Subject: CS: Canary orchestration + QMon execution plan

Sam / Priya —

Thanks for the kickoff this morning. As discussed, attaching our initial artifacts so we can lock the canary windows and validation gates: qmon-promptset-v1.csv (seed prompts), eval-harness-config.yaml (nightly job + metrics), and a mutual-action-plan.xlsx with milestones.

Quick asks before we schedule the canary: 
- Confirm preferred canary window (we suggested 02:00-06:00 PST to minimize user impact).
- Confirm the golden prompt set in the CSV — if you want changes, call them out by line number.
- Any compliance requirements for storing eval outputs (we default to 30 days for temporary logs).

High-level plan (short):
1) Nightly eval harness runs on a staging snapshot; regression alerts if model-quality delta > threshold.
2) Canary ramp 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48 hours with automated rollback gate.
3) Warmup traffic and KV cache priming during a 30-min buffer before each ramp step.

I'll put a concise playbook in Drive and send an invite for a 30-min alignment call after you confirm the window.

—Marissa

Thanks, looks good. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 
1) Alerts: what exact signal triggers a regression alert? We need a concrete definition for our on-call.
2) Can you confirm whether the nightly eval uses sampled production logs or a synthetic replay of interactions? We prefer a reproducible replay.
3) Timezone: the 02:00-06:00 window is fine for us, but can we do a shorter ramp during the first night (e.g., 5% -> 15%) and then full 25% the second night? We want to see a smaller blast radius first.

Also, Priya wants the rollback checklist before we go live. Can you share that separately?

Subject: Re: CS: Canary orchestration + QMon execution plan

Thanks, Sam — good questions. Short answers then concrete gates below.

1) Regression alert definition (team-friendly):
   - Primary quality metric: rerank F1 on golden set. Alert if nightly F1 drops by >= 3.0 percentage points vs baseline AND absolute F1 < 78.0.
   - Secondary signals (any one triggers page if primary is borderline): 24h bump in hallucination rate by > 7% (measured by keyword heuristics), or loss of end-to-end accuracy >= 4%.
   - Operational SLO gate: P95 latency increase > 200ms over baseline for 2 consecutive hourly buckets.

2) Eval harness: we will run a reproducible replay — ingest the provided seed examples and a snapshot of sanitized prod logs if you agree. By default, the harness runs nightly at 03:00 PST against the canary model and produces a JSON artifact retained for 30 days.

3) Canary ramp proposal (updated per your ask):
   Night 1: 5% for first 6 hours, if gates pass then 15% for remaining window.
   Night 2: 25% for full window.
   Full: move to 100% only after 48 hours with all gates green and manual sign-off.

Gates (automated rollback triggers):
- Any primary metric breach as defined above -> automatic rollback to previous model variant and alert channel.
- Sustained P95 latency > 750ms for more than one hour -> throttled rollback.
- Error rate spike (5xx) > 0.8% for 30 minutes -> immediate rollback.

Operational notes:
- We'll create a Slack channel #cs-acme-qmon and a PagerDuty escalation for after-hours.
- KV cache warmup: 30-min priming window before each ramp; we will pre-warm common prefixes.
- The eval harness config attached includes exact metric calculations and the path to the golden prompt identifiers.

I'll add the rollback checklist (Laura) and a short runbook to Drive. If this looks good I'll schedule the canary for Thu, Jan 18 02:00 PST.

—Marissa

Quick tech note from infra side: 
- Metric definitions in eval-harness-config.yaml use micro-averaged F1 for rerank and a separate hallucination detector (keyword + model score threshold). Make sure the customer is aware micro vs macro can move numbers slightly.
- Latency P95 threshold: Recommend hard guard at 750ms (as Marissa suggested) and a soft warning at 600ms.
- For rollback, we will tag model variants with git-like release tags (e.g., release/acme-2028-37-v2). Rollback will switch traffic and reclaim KV cache gracefully (no abrupt cache flush).

Ben
